title: At the Bottom of the Sea...
text:
At the bottom of the sea

there is a house of glass.


Onto an avenue

of madrepores

it opens.


A great golden fish,

at five o'clock,

comes to greet me.


It brings me

a red bouquet

of coral flowers.


I sleep in a bed

a little bluer

than the sea.


An octopus

winks at me

through the glass.

In the green forest

that surrounds me

—ding dong... ding dang—

there sway and sing

the mermaids

of sea-green mother-of-pearl.


And above my head

there burn, in the twilight,

the bristling tips of the sea.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the childlike underwater music and the crystalline house imagery.

title: Do You Remember?
text:
My mouth with a mischievous kiss

sought your traitorous swallows,

and I felt your captive eyelashes

beating in the curves of my kiss.


Matter freed me of its weight...

a blaze of springs passed through me

and the soul, anesthetized with chimeras,

knew the fruition of rapture.


It was a moment of peace so exquisite

that I sipped the light of infinity

and was assailed by the desire to weep.


Do you remember that the afternoon was dying

and while you whispered: "Mine! Mine!"

like a child I began to sob?...
editorial_note: The translation preserves the sonnet's move from erotic lightness into childlike sobbing.

title: Suggestion of a Willow
text:
There must exist a city of moss

whose sky of grays, at sunset,

is crossed by green angels with wings

fallen from frayed glass.

And cold mirrors in the grass

on whose edges, bent over, weep

long widows of yellowish wind

that the glass blurs as they sway.


And a point in the space of hanging

water weeds; and a dead girl

who goes thinking on clover feet.

And a grotto that sweetly rains

vegetable batrachians that shatter,

newborn leaves, on the soft silt.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the surreal botanic atmosphere and the unusual batrachian image.

title: Modern
text:
I will dance on a carpet of green,

have ready the wine in the ringing glass,

we shall drink the golden liquor

celebrating the night and its freshness.


I will dance like the pure earth,

like the earth I shall be a treasure,

and in giving myself pure I shall find no dishonor,

for giving oneself is a form of height.


I will dance so that you forget everything

and I shall give you the intoxication you ask

until Venus passes through the skies.


But perhaps something will be hidden from you,

for pagan woman of an impoverished century,

I shall not let all the veils fall.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the speaker's self-possession and the withheld final veil.

title: Divine Night
text:
This garden yields us its delight,

yields us the tree full of apples.

fountain of gods propitious to thirst,

bread of instinct, good for hunger.


But white marble of unequaled modesty

fixes on us its serene gaze:

bare thigh, the breast vigorous,

pure, like the light that caresses it.


Your eyes become too blue,

impalpable tulles cover your hands

and something divine lifts you in flight.


Let us not cut the delightful fruit

and look at the soul in a pink cloud,

how blue is the beatitude of heaven.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the tension between garden desire and marble restraint.

title: Transfusion
text:
Your life nourishes my blood

and I love you to death, I love you; if I could

under black skies I would eat

your heart with lioness teeth.


Before knowing you I was a thief

and now I am a diminished prisoner.

How well my spring shines!

How my crown gleams on your brow!


Blood that is mine burns in your pupils

and between your lips each afternoon places

the sweet grapes with which Pan invites.


And meanwhile; flower without air, flower in grotto,

I squeeze all myself into you like a fruit

and between your hands my life goes away.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the bodily extremity of love as blood, fruit, hunger, and possession.

title: Life
text:
My nerves are mad, in the veins

the blood boils, liquid fire

leaps to my lips where it then feigns

the joy of every festival.


I feel like laughing; the sorrows

that I do not summon at will,

today do not play with me and I play

with the blue sadness of which they are full.


The world beats; all its harmony

I feel so vibrant that I make it mine

when I pour from its sorceress ballad.


It is that I opened the window a moment ago

and on the finest wings of the wind

spring has brought me its sun.
editorial_note: The difficult middle phrase is rendered as active refusal, while the spring-window turn is kept clear.

title: I Am
text:
I am gentle and sad if I adore, I can

bring heaven down to my hand when

I entangle another's soul with mine.

You will find no down softer.


No one like me kisses hands,

nor crouches so much in a dream,

nor did there fit in another body, so small,

a human soul of greater tenderness.


I die upon the eyes, if I feel them

like living birds, for a moment,

flutter beneath my white fingers.


I know the phrase that enchants and understands

and I know how to be silent when the moon ascends

enormous and red over the ravines.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the tender self-portrait and the closing discipline of silence.

title: Tired Animal
text:
I want a fierce love of claw and tooth

that assaults me treacherously in broad daylight,

and that suffocates this pride of mine,

this pride of being all-powerful.


I want a fierce love of claw and tooth

that in raw flesh begins my bleeding,

to see if this melancholy ends

that slowly corrupts my soul.


I want a love that is a storm,

that breaks everything and stirs everything

because deep vigor feeds it.


So that there my clay may revive,

my poor clay of a tired animal,

sick of rolling along old paths.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated demand for a violent love and the final animal weariness.

title: I Want a Fierce Love of Claw and Tooth...
text:
I want a fierce love of claw and tooth

That assaults me treacherously in broad daylight,

And that suffocates this pride of mine,

This pride of being all-powerful.


I want a fierce love of claw and tooth

That in raw flesh begins my bleeding,

To see if this melancholy ends

That slowly corrupts my soul.


I want a love that is a storm,

That breaks everything and stirs everything

Because deep vigor feeds it.


So that there my clay may revive,

my poor clay of a tired animal,

Sick of rolling along old paths.
editorial_note: This related version preserves the source's capitalized line openings while matching the translated imagery.
